Rate people's various strengths and weaknesses in many different areas as objectively as you can manage, and then only sterilize the overall bottom one percent or so of the population. This would promote evolution toward attributes that society values, but on the downside, evolution without predators promotes variation which while seemingly negative in the short term, may develop into beneficial variations later. People are quite biased in what they value as beneficial. What is beneficial in the future may not be the same as what has generally been thought of as beneficial in the past. Genetically, the surest bet is to have as varied a gene pool as possible, which means having both specialization and generalization. What I would advocate would be to breed portions of the population in different ways so that we have both specialized and generalized branches of humanity. Hell, we could even have branches of genetic defects, and breed them back to vitality. The wrong number of chromosomes is currently bad, but if we bred people with the wrong number of chromosomes, we might be able to develop viable parallel branches of our species that might develop into their own intelligent capable species with their own strengths and weaknesses compared to our own. It would also be good to vary culture in similar ways, having some specialized cultures, some organic cultures, and some cultures with different moral values, some that value multiculturalism, and some that value homogeneity, without trying to force the others to be the same.
